source_name: arhiva.finance.gov.mk — Огласи и договори за јавни набавки (archived MK Ministry of Finance procurement notices)
why_relevant: An officially maintained MK-side ARCHIVE domain preserving procurement notices and contracts that have been removed from the current finance.gov.mk estate. Exactly the class of retained-but-delisted material this cell is chartered to find.

source_name: nabavke.com — regional tender database (RS, ME, BA, MK, HR, SI)
why_relevant: Commercial regional aggregator that explicitly advertises Macedonia among its covered markets alongside Serbia, Montenegro, BiH, Croatia and Slovenia. Regional aggregators retain notices after national-portal expiry and normalise them across borders — useful for spotting the same vendor/spec appearing in several NLB or Sparkasse markets.

source_name: eKapija Tenderi — regional public procurement portal (RS/ME/BA + 16 further countries incl. Macedonia)
why_relevant: Established Serbian-market aggregator whose 'about' page claims coverage extending to Macedonia, Slovenia, Croatia, Bulgaria and Greece. Its regional breadth makes it a candidate for detecting a parent-group framework contract surfacing simultaneously in several Balkan markets.

source_name: EBRD Client e-Procurement Portal (ECEPP) + EBRD procurement notices
why_relevant: Cross-border IFI channel. EBRD is both a lender to and (historically) a shareholder in MK banks (e.g. a 25% stake in TTK), and EBRD-financed goods/works/consultancy contracts in North Macedonia are notified via ECEPP rather than the MK national portal — a procurement stream invisible to anyone watching e-nabavki alone.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (EU OJ supplement; subset covers North Macedonia)
why_relevant: The TED dataset explicitly extends beyond the EEA to include the Republic of North Macedonia, and TED is where EU-side parent entities' high-value notices and award notices appear. It is simultaneously a cross-border source and a permanent archive of award notices.

source_name: TendersInfo — Balkan region tenders / contract awards
why_relevant: English-language commercial aggregator with a dedicated Balkan-region view including a separate contract-awards section. Its value here is regional cross-referencing and award-notice retention, not primary authority — items are republished, so provenance must always be traced back to the national source.

source_name: GlobalTenders / TendersOnTime — Balkans and EBRD-funded tender feeds
why_relevant: Second-tier commercial aggregators with Balkan and funding-agency (EBRD) cross-sections. Useful mainly as a redundancy layer: if a notice vanished from the MK portal but was mirrored by one of these, the metadata survives.

source_name: Neighbouring national procurement portals (RS jnportal, BA javnenabavke.gov.ba, ME cejn.gov.me)
why_relevant: NLB operates subsidiary banks in Serbia, BiH, Montenegro and Kosovo alongside Skopje. Where a group vendor is engaged through a public-sector-adjacent entity in a neighbouring market, the notice is published on that country's portal. Comparing sibling-market notices exposes group framework agreements that are never separately tendered in MK.

source_name: Macedonian Stock Exchange (MSE) issuer disclosures — TTK Banka and other listed MK banks
why_relevant: Reveals-indirectly source: listed MK banks must disclose material contracts and ownership changes. Ownership shifts (e.g. a foreign parent acquiring a stake) are the precondition for procurement decision-making moving abroad, and MSE filings are the authoritative record of when that happened.

source_name: ProCredit Holding AG — corporate procurement policy and group disclosures
why_relevant: Pointer to the Frankfurt-based parent of ProCredit Bank AD Skopje and to the group's Corporate Procurement Policy principles (transparency, equality, cost-effectiveness, responsibility; 'value for money' supplier selection) that govern MK-level buying. Use it to reach the authoritative holding-company estate and its annual/impact reports.

source_name: Биро за јавни набавки (Public Procurement Bureau, BJN)
why_relevant: Regulator/administrator of the procurement system: publishes manuals for ESJN, methodology, statistics and analytics on procurement across all contracting authorities including the central bank. Key for understanding how NBRNM notices are structured and where fields live.

source_name: TED / EU Publications Office notice — NBRNM coins procurement
why_relevant: Confirms NBRNM publishes above-threshold notices to EU-visible channels (a coins supply notice, CPV 18512100, 2 lots, published 05/03/2024, deadline 29/03/2024, electronic submission via e-nabavki). Gives an English-language, structured mirror of Macedonian central-bank tenders.

source_name: НБРСМ — Платни системи и платежни услуги (payment systems hub)
why_relevant: The regulator-side half of this dual cell: hub page for payment systems policy, oversight and the payment infrastructure. Anchors the MIPS, oversight-role, regulation and payment-statistics subpages that signal infrastructure modernisation (and therefore future tenders).

source_name: НБРСМ — МИПС (Macedonian Interbank Payment System) page
why_relevant: MIPS is the RTGS system owned and operated by NBRNM; this page carries system rules, participation and self-assessment material. RTGS modernisation and instant-payments work are the direct upstream of central-bank IT/infrastructure tenders.

source_name: НБРСМ — Регулатива за платните системи и платежните услуги
why_relevant: Consolidated bylaws and decisions (e.g. Одлука за критериумите за класификација на платните системи и стандардите за нивното работење) that define licensing obligations, technical standards and guarantee-mechanism requirements — the rulebook that shapes vendor requirements.

source_name: НБРСМ — Платежна статистика (payment statistics)
why_relevant: Time series on card, terminal, ATM/POS and credit-transfer volumes plus the annual information on payment developments — the demand-side indicator set that explains why and when infrastructure procurement happens.

source_name: НБРСМ — КИБС oversight page (licensed payment system operator)
why_relevant: The central bank's own page describing KIBS as the operator of the deferred multilateral net settlement system for retail payments — the regulator-side record of an authorised operator, and the hook for licensing decisions (KIBS obtained an instant-credit-transfer operator licence on 17.9.2025).

source_name: ЈП Службен весник на РСМ (Official Gazette)
why_relevant: Legally authoritative publication venue for NBRNM decisions (including payment-system classification/standards decisions and reporting obligations) and for procurement-law amendments. The canonical dated text behind every regulatory change relevant to this cell.

source_name: НБРСМ портал (portal.nbrm.gov.mk) — application/reporting portal
why_relevant: A separate National Bank portal domain surfaced in search; likely the e-services / reporting entry point for supervised entities. Worth mapping because it may expose public sub-registers or forms that reveal reporting taxonomies (and therefore data the bank holds).

source_name: Commercial tender aggregators covering North Macedonia (tenderdetail, tender-service, tendersinfo, selltostate/Hook)
why_relevant: English-language mirrors/alerting layers over ESJN. Useful as a cross-check and for early alerting, but they are derivative, often incomplete, and paywalled — never a substitute for ESJN itself.

source_name: МДТ портал за документи (portal.mdt.gov.mk)
why_relevant: Document repository of the ministry; observed hosting State Audit Office reports on MDT itself. Likely also hosts procurement plans, project documentation and strategy papers that name systems and vendors.

source_name: МДТ — TrustEID (trusteid.mdt.gov.mk)
why_relevant: National trust services / eID programme run by MDT. Trust-service and eID infrastructure is directly adjacent to payments authentication (SCA, qualified certificates) and reveals which vendors/CAs are engaged.

source_name: МДТ — Broadband Competence Office (bco.mdt.gov.mk)
why_relevant: Programme office under MDT; useful mainly as a pointer to EU-funded digital infrastructure programmes and their procurement pipelines, and to MDT's project-office structure.
